activities.caption: file the traffic — free or paid?
activities.name: mtTrafficBuckets

config.prompt: The membrane's traffic splits by one question: is the cell paying for it? File each case:

items.label: diffusion — the molecules' own random motion does the work
active transport — uphill, against the gradient
protein carriers changing shape using ATP
glucose hauled uphill in the gut

config.why: Diffusion and osmosis cost nothing; active transport runs uphill and is billed in ATP — the cell's small coins.

activities.caption: pair each factor with its design instruction
activities.name: mtFactorsMatch

config.prompt: Four factors set the rate — pair each with how anatomy exploits it:

pairs.right: keep it steep — blood sweeps CO₂ off the lung side the moment it crosses
warmer molecules collide more — labs incubate cultures warm
fold it — 300 million alveoli pack ~70 m² into your chest
minimise it — the villain of the piece

config.why: Maximise area and gradient, minimise distance, keep the medium moving — every exchange organ is a variation on the same four-factor theme.

activities.anchor: diffusion stops once equilibrium is reached
activities.caption: true or false — life at equilibrium
activities.name: mtEquilibJudge

statements.s: What stops at equilibrium is the net movement; individual molecules keep crossing both ways in equal numbers.
statements.why: Equilibrium is dynamic — a balanced interchange, not a standstill.

statements.s: Real cells rarely reach equilibrium anyway, because they consume what arrives and replace what leaves.
statements.why: Holding the gradient alive is the cell's whole trick.

statements.s: Once equilibrium is reached, individual molecules stop moving.
statements.why: Only the NET movement stops — the crossings continue exactly as before, in equal numbers.

statements.s: Diffusion is the net movement from lower to higher concentration.
statements.why: Down the gradient, always — uphill is active transport's paid job.

activities.anchor: Water is the solvent of life
activities.caption: fill the blanks — osmosis, defined
activities.name: mtOsmosisCloze

config.text: Osmosis is the net movement of %%0%% molecules from a %%1%% solution to a %%2%% one, through a %%3%% %%4%% membrane — and water always moves from higher water potential to lower.
config.hint: The membrane holds the solute back — that withheld solute is what creates the water-potential difference.

activities.caption: pin the isotonic point on the concentration scale
activities.name: mtIsotonicPlace

config.prompt: Potato strips soaked in sucrose solutions: the length-change line crosses zero where the tissue neither gains nor loses water. Pin that concentration (mol/dm³):
config.why: About 0.3 mol/dm³ for potato — the plot is a calibration: any unknown solution can now be matched against the tissue.
config.context: Dialysis tubing works the same way: fill it with strong sugar solution, weigh it, and watch the mass climb as water enters.

activities.caption: dilute solution, two fates — drag between kingdoms
activities.name: mtStakesCompare

config.prompt: A dilute solution floods in — drag the divider between the two kingdoms:

before.label: animal cell (no wall)
before.text: A red blood cell swells until it bursts — haemolysis. Which is why intravenous drips are precisely 0.9% saline.

after.label: plant cell (wall)
after.text: The vacuole swells and the cytoplasm presses outward on the cellulose wall — turgid. A crisp lettuce is a hydraulic structure.

config.why: In concentrated solution the fates reverse — shrivelled for the wall-less, plasmolysed for the walled — and guard cells open stomata by the same pump-free trick.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the membrane-engineering answer
activities.name: mtSteerSpot

config.prompt: This cell-traffic answer contains one faulty line — click it:
lines: Diffusion only runs downhill; active transport pumps uphill against the gradient.
Protein carriers pick up their cargo, change shape using ATP, and release it on the far side.
Poison the mitochondria and active transport stops within minutes, while diffusion carries on.
A cell can steer individual diffusing molecules directly to where they are needed.
Wherever a cell accumulates a substance against the gradient, expect mitochondria crowded around that membrane.
config.correction: A cell cannot steer individual molecules — it can only shape the conditions: maintaining gradients, installing channels and carriers, moving the membrane itself.
config.why: Diffusion is nobody's employee; the membrane's architecture is the cell's only lever — which is why so much of cell biology is really membrane engineering.

activities.caption: call the magnitude — the idling engine's pace
activities.name: mtPumpEstimate

config.prompt: The sodium–potassium pump spends one ATP per cycle, exporting 3 Na⁺ and importing 2 K⁺. Roughly how many cycles does one pump run per second?
config.why: About 1,000 times per second per pump — tens of millions per neuron, consuming a third to a half of the brain's energy budget.
config.context: Resting potential — the 70 mV every neuron holds — is this pump's accumulated work: active transport as the idling engine of the nervous system.
